correctness.rationale: The stationary one-site age is Exp(r) independent of the excursion, and the zero-initial immigration law at age t has PGF [1+B_t(1−s)]^(−Aζ/(vl)) with B_t=l(1−e^(−Δt))/Δ. This can be recovered by Poisson superposition of one-founder birth–death trees, for which 1−F_t(s)=(1−s)e^(−Δt)/(1+B_t(1−s)); integrating over founder arrival time gives the logarithm. The product of v age-averaged PGFs yields (1) with a proper PGF continuous at 1. Admissibility gives 1−βJζ≥1−βJ0>0, while 0<ν<1 bounds the density integrals by an integrable multiple of x^(−ν). The finite critical mean is the level integral of A0/(x+r). The conditional scaling lemma applies at fixed interior fitness after v→∞ and ζ↓0 (not δ→0), then x↓0: at s=e^(−ur), B_(t/r)(1−s)→ut with bound ut and A0/l→1. The limit is a proper continuous-at-zero Laplace transform, with no mass at zero by its decay as u→∞. Differentiating the log transform at zero gives first three cumulants 1,2,12, hence raw moments 1,3,19. For the full occupation, the k-th factorial cumulant satisfies r^k κ_k^(F)≤A0 l^(k−1) k!(k−1)! because B_(t/r)≤lt/r. Products in the factorial-moment Bell polynomials and the bounded factor r≤C for unused degrees give a uniform bound on E[(rN_x)^k], for every integer k. In the uniform fitness integral substitute y=nCx^ν; the transformed integrand is dominated by y^(a−1)min(1,M_k/y^k) for k>a. The conditional limit yields convergence at almost every y (countably many possible discontinuities suffice). Layer cake gives the exact mixed amplitude C^(−a) E[Y^a] and the divergent moment at p=a. The repaired finding narrows novelty to this unconditional asymptotic and its moment frontier; all original formulas used in the proof remain mathematically valid.
residual_risks: Sequential independent-state mean-field limit only, not a simultaneous or finite-system critical theorem. The endpoint l=1 is excluded. Uniform fitness-level selection is essential to the coefficient and exponent, and is not sampling by q or size bias.

evidence: The one-founder mass integrates without reset weighting to l^n/(ln), so nΛ_n≤(A0/l)l^n. In the scaled Laplace exponent rn≤ε contributes O(ε); rn>M contributes O(1/M) by rE[N_x]≤sup A0. The cutoff therefore gives the conditional Laplace integral by compact Riemann sums. For the unconditional tail, the changed-variable integral requires domination by uniformly bounded higher moments of rN_x; the mean or the pointwise conditional cutoff alone cannot control it when 1/ν>1.

value.rationale: Uniform fitness-level total occupancy is the natural random-vertex observable of the stated level model, not a selected moment or an arbitrary tiny case. Mean condensation theory leaves open how often a level has a large load in the finite-mean regime. The exact mixture coefficient and complete positive-moment frontier quantify it, requiring control of aggregate occupation rather than a single founder or within-site pair count. The conditional lemma is useful in the proof but is not a separate value claim.
residual_risks: No finite-network asymptotics or claims for other sampling measures, dependent sites or global resetting.
